text: Correct: this abbreviation is O(P)/m(P), using the maximal ideal of the actual valuation ring, as in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Constants map into O(P) and then reduce, supplying the intended k-algebra structure. It is a field even when F/k is not a function field; finite dimension over k is a separate theorem. The [explicit quadratic residue equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/XSqAddOne.lean#L68) and its generator equation identify the residue field with k(i), hence Q(i) over Q. The [infinity residue equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Basic.lean#L217) gives k, so the two required residue types are distinguished. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L490).
The native quadratic residue-field equivalence sends the class of X to i and specializes over Q to the prescribed Q(i) control.
The actual infinity residue field has degree one, with its canonical k-algebra equivalence constructed immediately afterward.

Correct: `IsFunctionField` already asserts a transcendental x together with finiteness over k(x); the conclusion retains that witness and forgets only the finiteness conjunct. This is the existence inherent in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). It does not claim that a nonconstant element over a non-exact base is necessarily transcendental. The [native RatFunc proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L115) supplies X, so the hypothesis is nonvacuous and the witness is the actual field coordinate. No canonical choice of parameter or extra constant-field assumption is asserted. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L58).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.

Correct: every transcendental y in a one-variable function field is another rational parameter, so F is finite-dimensional over the actual intermediate field k⟮y⟯. This is [Stichtenoth, Remark 1.1.2](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The proof exchanges the original parameter x and y through k(x,y), then uses finite-dimensionality in a tower. The explicit `Transcendental k y` hypothesis is essential: an element algebraic over enlarged constants need not be a parameter. The [residue-finiteness proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Degree.lean#L226) genuinely applies this result to a uniformizer, while [RatFunc supplies the initial parameter](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L115). Separability and exact constants are unnecessary. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L62).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.
The actual place-residue finiteness proof uses this parameter-exchange result on a uniformizer proven transcendental.

Correct: a finite extension E/F of a function field F/k remains finite over a rational subfield of F, hence is a function field over k. This is the finite-tower consequence of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean retains `FiniteDimensional F E` and the compatible scalar tower, and does not add separability. Its proof combines finite generation with unchanged transcendence degree. The finite hypothesis matters: an arbitrary algebraic extension only receives the weaker transcendence-degree statement elsewhere. The [constructed quadratic function field](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Hyperelliptic/Genus/Two.lean#L119) supplies a native finite-extension control; characteristic-two inseparability is not excluded from its function-field assertion. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L183).
The actual quadratic y²=x⁵−1 field is a function field in every characteristic; separability is only added later for the different.

Correct: the witness is the actual rational coordinate `RatFunc.X`. Its transcendence is proved, and `RatFunc.adjoin_X` identifies k⟮X⟯ with the whole rational function field, making the remaining extension degree one. Thus the conclusion realizes [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html) for every field k. It does not rely on k being infinite, perfect or algebraically closed. The roadmap’s rational object is used concretely in the [polynomial-space dimension computation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/RatFunc.lean#L152) ℓ(nP∞)=n+1 and the degree-one infinity place, which guard against an unintended rational-function carrier. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L115).
The native RatFunc object has the explicitly computed polynomial Riemann–Roch space dimension n+1.
The actual rational-coordinate infinity place has residue degree one.

Correct: this algebra structure is the original map k→F with codomain restricted to O(P), using that all constants are integral at P. It is the constants inclusion underlying [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The following [coercion equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L482) shows that a constant sent into O(P) and then back to F is unchanged, so the instance introduces no competing scalar action. It includes zero and works without a function-field or exact-constants hypothesis. Reduction of this map supplies the k-algebra structure used in the [native quadratic residue equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/XSqAddOne.lean#L68). [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L475).
The constructed constants algebra map followed by inclusion into F equals the original algebraMap k F.
The native quadratic residue-field equivalence sends the class of X to i and specializes over Q to the prescribed Q(i) control.

Correct: if F is finite over some k(x) and algebraic over an intermediate field E, then E has transcendence degree one over k. A transcendental element of E is a parameter for F, and E is a subspace of that finite extension, proving finite dimension over its own rational subfield. The algebraic hypothesis and compatible tower are explicit. This combines the [transcendence-degree tower law](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/030H) with the parameter property in [Stichtenoth, Remark 1.1.2](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html); it does not incorrectly assume every algebraic extension is finite. The identity case E=F and the native rational-field case are valid. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L205).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.

Correct: every constant belongs to the valuation ring because the place is trivial on k: nonzero constants have valuation one, and zero has valuation zero. Both are ≤1, the ring’s defining bound. This is the constants inclusion of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.4](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The claim is literal membership of `algebraMap k F c` in O(P), with no assumption that c is nonzero or that k is the exact constant field. The [algebra-map coherence equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L482) confirms the same inclusion supplies the scalar structure; the [non-exact C(x)/R example](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/RealComplex.lean#L28) remains allowed. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L321).
The constants-membership proof gives the canonical constants algebra map, whose inclusion back into F is unchanged.
The source constructs the genuine non-exact extension C(x)/R as a function field and computes ℓ(0)=2; exact constants cannot be inferred.

Correct: two normalized places with the same valuation subring have equivalent valuations, and surjectivity onto the fixed discrete value group makes those valuations equal. Thus injectivity identifies actual places, not merely equivalence classes. This agrees with [Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.1.13](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Normalization is essential; arbitrary positive rescalings would share a ring without sharing their numerical valuation. The [rational-coordinate membership test](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Basic.lean#L360) separates infinity from every finite place, giving a concrete check of the map being compared. No function-field assumption is needed once normalized places are supplied. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L444).
The actual rational coordinate is outside the valuation ring precisely at infinity, checking the regular/pole distinction.

Correct: membership in `P.integers` unfolds exactly to `P.valuation f ≤ 1`, the multiplicative form of the valuation-ring condition in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.4](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The inequality is in the right direction: poles have value greater than one. Zero is included because its multiplicative value is zero; no nonzero premise is needed. The [native X membership theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Basic.lean#L360) makes infinity the unique place where X fails this condition, while x⁻¹ has order one there. This statement exposes the actual subring predicate without changing its mathematical content. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L139).
The actual rational coordinate is outside the valuation ring precisely at infinity, checking the regular/pole distinction.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: if every coefficient from R maps into O(P), a monic equation over R becomes one over O(P); the valuation ring's integral closedness then puts its root y in O(P). This is the normality statement in [Stacks, Lemma 10.50.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8). Lean requires image containment, not an injective R→F map, so arbitrary commutative R is appropriate. The proof constructs precisely that restricted scalar map before applying integral closedness. Zero is allowed. The published [algebraic-constants membership result](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L340) confirms that enlarged constants remain regular, without imposing exact constants. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L459).
Every element of the actual relative algebraic closure belongs to the valuation ring; this is the constants-integrality boundary case.

Correct: for nonzero f and g with different orders, the smaller order survives in f+g, matching [Stichtenoth, Lemma 1.1.11](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Unequal orders exclude cancellation, so a separate f+g≠0 premise is unnecessary. Both nonzero premises are nevertheless needed because Lean defines ord(0)=0; dropping one could make the asserted minimum wrong. Equal-order cancellation is deliberately outside the statement, in every characteristic. The published [order computation for cXᵃ(X−1)ᵇ at infinity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Order.lean#L213) gives −(a+b), and the native x⁻¹ order is one, checking the sign convention used here. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L265).
The existing native family computes order at infinity as −(a+b), with the actual X−1 factor retaining the pole order of X.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: an element algebraic over k has order zero at every place trivial on k; the contrapositive therefore makes any element of nonzero order transcendental. This is the constant-field behavior described by [Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.1.13](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The hypothesis also excludes f=0 because its assigned order is zero. No function-field or exact-constants hypothesis is needed. The published [residue-finiteness proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Degree.lean#L226) actually applies this theorem to a uniformizer, then uses that transcendental element as a rational parameter. The native x⁻¹ uniformizer at infinity provides a concrete nonvacuous instance. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L337).
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.
The source actually applies transcendental_of_ord_ne_zero to a uniformizer before invoking the finite-dimensional parameter theorem.

Correct: the multiplicative valuation equals exp(−ord), translating the additive discrete valuation of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html) into Lean's ordered multiplicative group. Here exp is the formal group identification, not the real exponential. The nonzero guard is essential: v(0)=0 but exp(−ord(0))=1. The minus sign makes positive order mean valuation below one and poles mean valuation above one. The actual [infinity formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Basic.lean#L122) gives v∞(f)=exp(intDegree f), while x⁻¹ has order one there. These published formulas check both normalization and orientation. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L156).
The native infinity valuation is exp(intDegree f) for nonzero f, agreeing with the negated additive-order convention.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: adjoining one transcendental parameter is finitely generated as a field extension, and a finite extension of it is again finitely generated. Lean's `Algebra.EssFiniteType` is the appropriate field-generation condition, as confirmed by the pinned [proof through intermediate-field generation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L93); it does not assert finite dimension over k or finite generation as a k-algebra. This is a direct consequence of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The native rational-function case supplies the one-generator field, and the constructed C(x)/R control shows that exact constants are not being silently imposed. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L92).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.
The source constructs the genuine non-exact extension C(x)/R as a function field and computes ℓ(0)=2; exact constants cannot be inferred.

Correct: the defining rational subfield k(x) has transcendence degree one, and F/k(x) is algebraic because it is finite. The [transcendence-degree tower law](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/030H) therefore gives trdegₖ(F)=1. Lean uses cardinal-valued `Algebra.trdeg`, and this finite value is an actual rank statement, not `finrank`'s zero value on infinite-dimensional spaces. The published rational-coordinate construction supplies a genuine model. The non-exact C(x)/R example remains valid: its enlarged algebraic constants change degrees and ℓ(0), but not transcendence degree. No converse without finite generation is claimed. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L105).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.
The source constructs the genuine non-exact extension C(x)/R as a function field and computes ℓ(0)=2; exact constants cannot be inferred.

Correct: for an algebraic extension E/F, the [tower formula](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/030H) adds trdeg_F(E)=0 to trdegₖ(F)=1. Lean keeps the compatible k→F→E scalar tower explicit and permits infinite algebraic extensions. The conclusion is only transcendence degree one; it does not incorrectly declare E a finitely generated function field. The separate [finite-extension theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L183) adds the finite-degree hypothesis for that stronger conclusion. The native rational field and the existing quadratic function-field construction provide the finite cases without introducing a separability restriction. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L172).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.
The actual quadratic function-field construction provides the finite-extension control; the present theorem additionally allows infinite algebraic extensions.

Correct: F is algebraic over the embedded commutative k-algebra E, so E and F have the same algebraic-independence rank over k. Lean's `FaithfulSMul E F` ensures that E really embeds; since F is a field, E is a domain. This is the domain version of the [transcendence-degree tower law](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/030H), proved in the pinned Mathlib by combining transcendence bases. E need not itself be a field or finitely generated, and neither conclusion is asserted. The [following field-descent theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L205) adds a field assumption before proving the stronger function-field property. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L193).
The published downstream field-descent theorem actually uses this transcendence-degree result, while separately imposing Field E for its stronger conclusion.
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.

Correct: Mathlib's `FunctionField k F` means finite dimension over a specified RatFunc k algebra, while Tau Ceti's predicate chooses a transcendental parameter intrinsically. With the stated compatible embedding, its image of X is transcendental and its field range is exactly k⟮image X⟯. Parameter exchange then proves the forward implication; the reverse uses that same image of X. This matches [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html) without making a chosen embedding part of the intrinsic notion. The source explicitly proves the range equality, so it compares the actual scalar structures rather than merely isomorphic field types. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L131).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.
The actual parameter-exchange theorem applies to the image of RatFunc.X under the specified embedding; it supplies the essential forward implication.

Correct: among finitely generated field extensions, transcendence degree one is equivalent to being finite over a rational subfield. The forward direction is the [tower law](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/030H); conversely a transcendental x leaves algebraic degree over k(x), and finite generation upgrades that algebraic extension to finite dimension. Lean explicitly retains `Algebra.EssFiniteType k F`, so infinite algebraic extensions of k(x) are not accidentally included. The proof handles cardinal cancellation at the finite value one before applying algebraic finite generation. Native RatFunc and the non-exact C(x)/R example check that neither separability nor exact constants has been added. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L153).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.
